Subject: Request: temporary log-retention exception + evidence for backup purge window

Hi Rishi / Soojin,

We ran into a customer audit requirement that compels us to request a short, controlled retention exception for system logs that would otherwise be pruned in Redwood's scheduled backup purge on 2026-06-10. The auditor is asking for preserved request/response logs covering a specific 48-hour span (2026-05-27 00:00 UTC to 2026-05-28 23:59 UTC) to investigate a data lineage issue.

We need:
- Confirmation that those logs can be held and not purged during the upcoming backup job.
- A list of subprocessors (and where those logs may be replicated) for the affected services.
- Evidence: retention manifest / checksum / sample log extract (redacted) showing custody.

This is time sensitive — auditor notified me this morning and expects a formal reply by EOD Friday (2026-06-04). Can Redwood provide a temporary hold and the requested artifacts? If this requires a DPA addendum or procurement sign-off, please advise next steps and owner.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of Security Ops
Luma Health

(attachment: luma_evidence_request_20260602.pdf)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lumahealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log-retention exception + evidence for backup purge window

Hi Daniel — thanks for the heads up and the clear list. We're on it. Quick plan and asks below.

1) Temporary hold: We have an emergency retention path for cases like this. We can prevent the purge for the specific object key range you identify and mark those snapshots as "forensic-hold" so they won't be deleted by the 2026-06-10 job. To do this we'll need the exact time range + service identifiers (model/service name + shard) and an internal ticket.

2) Subprocessor inventory: Olivia (cc) will pull the subprocessor replication mapping and any cross-region copies. Expect a short CSV.

3) Evidence artifacts: we can provide:
   - Retention manifest (date, object keys, storage location)
   - Hash/checksum for each preserved snapshot
   - A redacted sample log extract (PII removed)

4) DPA/contract: Holding logs temporarily for a customer request does not typically require a DPA amendment; however, if Luma needs Redwood to escrow or transfer custody to a third party, procurement/legal will need to sign an addendum.

Action items: please reply with
- the exact object keys or sequence IDs you want preserved (or we can preserve the whole service/object prefix if you prefer),
- whether you need the artifacts delivered to you or to the auditor directly (and if so, a delivery acceptance contact),
- whether Luma requests a standing exception or a one-time forensic hold.

I'll open SEC-4121 and tag Legal/PG to expedite. If you need the hold before EOD tomorrow, tell me and I'll escalate to infra oncall.

—Rishi
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

We can: 
- Place a forensic hold on the S3 prefix you specify immediately (no DPA change required).
- Produce a manifest + SHA256 checksums for each object retained.
- Produce a redacted sample for auditor inspection.

Legal note: if the auditor requires Redwood to attest to custody across subprocessors (signed affirmation), Legal will need to review the exact wording. We can provide a standard evidence packet; if Luma requires additional attestation language we will need a short addendum.

Proposed timeline:
- 2026-06-03 EOD: identify keys/confirm delivery target
- 2026-06-04 1200 UTC: manifest + checksum delivered to Luma secure drop
- 2026-06-10: scheduled purge skipped for forensic-hold objects; normal retention resumes after 30 days unless extended

If you confirm keys today we will escalate and lock them down.
